definition: A response delivery mode where a language model's output is sent incrementally, token by token or in small chunks, as it's generated, rather than waiting for the complete response.
details: Streaming significantly improves perceived responsiveness in interactive applications like chat interfaces, allowing users to start reading a response before the model has finished generating it entirely.

explainer.lead: Streaming is a delivery mode in LLM APIs where output is sent token by token or in small chunks as it is generated, instead of waiting for the whole response. It matters because users of interactive apps can start reading almost immediately.

tiers.eli5: Like a waiter bringing dishes one at a time as they're ready, instead of making you wait until the whole meal is cooked.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers enable streaming to improve perceived responsiveness in chat interfaces, handling chunks as they arrive rather than one blocking call. Pitfall: partial output complicates error handling, buffering and any post-processing that expects a complete response.
tiers.paperLevel: A response delivery mode in which a language model's output is sent incrementally, token by token or in small chunks, as it is generated rather than after completion.

explainer.example: A chat app shows the model's reply appearing word by word, so the user begins reading before generation has finished.
